To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the in vivo effects of aminooxy acetic acid on vitamin B6 vitamer concentration are different between synaptosomal and extrasynaptosomal fractions of brain.

SC decreased the levels of pyridoxic acid in synaptosomal plasma and PMP in extrasynaptosmal and synaptosomal mitochondrial fractions, while AOAA decreased the levels of PMP in extrasnaptosomal and synptosomal mitochondrial fractions.

the administration of semicarbazide decreased levels of pyrioxal phosphate in extrasynaptosmal and synaptosomal plasm, while the administration of aminooxyacetate more significantly decreased pyrioxamine phosphate levels in extrasynapotomal and synaptosomal mitochonria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of SC and AOAO on B6 vitamers in mouse brain.
the in vivo effects of AOAA and SC on B6 vitamers in mouse brain.
the effects of SC and/or AOAA on vitamin concentrations in brain subfractions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of AOAA and SC in the in vivo systems were not identical to those in the in vitro systems, but were rather similar to those in the isolated mitochondria.
the in vivo effect of AOAA on the PMP levels in the brain is greater than that of SC on the PLP levels.
AOAA and SC are inhibitors of PLP-enzymes and PMP-enzymes, respectively, and that AOAA and semicarbazidase are inhibitors of PMP-enzymatic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SC and AOAA, as inhibitors of PLP- and PMP-dependent enzymes, respectively, are useful tools to investigate the distribution of vitamin B6-enzyme activities in the subcellular fractions.
the effect of AOAA on vitamin-B6 metabolism in the brain is more marked on the mitochondria than on the plasma, while that of SC is more marked on plasma than on the mitochondria.

AOAA is a more specific inhibitor for PLP-dependent enzymes in the mitochondria than for those in the plasma, while SC is a specific inhibitor for PL-dependent enzymes in the plasma, but not in the mitochondria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SC decreases PLP levels by inhibiting the synthesis of PLP in extrasynaptosmal and synaptosomal membranes, whereas AOAA decreases PMP levels by inhibiting its synthesis in the mitochondria.

the difference between the in vivo effects of these two compounds on vitamin B6 enzymes is due to the difference in the distribution of vitamin B6 vitamers in brain subcellula fractions, especially in synaptosomal and extrasynaptosomal fractions.
AOAA and SC have different effects in vivo.
